In case you missed it, R6: Dees hop over Roos, three clubs STILL winless

All the headlines and major talking points from AFLW round six
By Staff writers
 Sep 20, 2026, 8:43 pm
Jorja Livingstone during round six between Melbourne and Carlton at Casey Fields, September 19, 2026. Picture: AFL Photos

CHECK out what we saw in round six of the 2026 season.
Roos' run done! Hawks' stunning upset ends North's amazing record

HAWTHORN'S women are giant killers, ending the longest winning streak in AFLW, AFL and VFL history.
Applying relentless pressure, the Hawks ground down two-time defending AFLW premier North Melbourne on Friday night for a seven-point triumph in Cairns, 4.8 (32) to 3.7 (25).

The Kangaroos' previous loss was the 2023 Grand Final. They opened 2024 with a win and a draw, before starting their historic 32-game winning streak.
This is Hawthorn's greatest AFLW win since it joined the league in 2022.

AFLW Highlights: Collingwood v Geelong
The Magpies and Cats clash in round six of the 2026 NAB AFLW Season

After a fast start from Georgie Prespakis through the middle – recording six clearances for the opening term – despite carrying a Carly Remmos tag, the Pies opted to shift stalwart Brit Bonnici (11 disposals, six tackles, one goal) to her.
The AFLW's original tagger, Bonnici certainly minimised Prespakis' freedom around the contest, but both continued to get productive across the ground.

MATCH REPORT
 Classy Cats crank it up to blow away winless Pies
Dees take top spot with strong win against Blues

MELBOURNE has continued its unbeaten run in 2026, with a dominant third term the key to setting up the 34-point victory against Carlton at Casey Fields on Saturday.
The Demons, playing against the Blues for the first time since 2022, kicked four goals to one in ‘the premiership quarter’ to take the game away from their opponents en route to winning 8.10 (58) to 3.6 (24).

AFLW Highlights: Melbourne v Carlton
The Demons and Blues clash in round six of the 2026 NAB AFLW Season

Tyla Hanks was everywhere, collecting a game-high 32 possessions and a goal, getting strong support from Olivia Purcell (26 and two).
Melbourne dominated disposals (+49), inside 50s (+18), and contested possessions (+24) to hand Carlton a second consecutive defeat.

MATCH REPORT
 Dees take top spot with strong win against Blues
Molloy lifts Swans to shake off dogged Power

THREE goals to Sydney superstar Chloe Molloy in her 75th  AFLW game propelled the Swans to an impressive 14-point win against Port Adelaide at Alberton Oval on Saturday.
Home fans were keen to celebrate Justine Mules-Robinson’s 100th - game milestone, but the visitors finally shook loose the dogged Power with the only two goals of the last quarter to spoil the party.

AFLW Highlights: Port Adelaide v Sydney
The Power and Swans clash in round six of the 2026 NAB AFLW Season

With Sydney midfield dynamo Sofia Hurley absent after undergoing ankle surgery, Zippy Fish spent more time at the stoppages, and she took full advantage to finish with a team-high 26 touches.
Playing her 50th game, Port star Abbey Dowrick was on record pace with 10 tackles in the first half. She slowed in the second to finish with 12, but was influential throughout with a game-high 27 possessions.

Dogs down Dockers to leapfrog into the eight

THE WESTERN Bulldogs have leapfrogged Fremantle to jump back into the top eight after winning a wind-affected match 6.4 (40) to 4.6 (30) on Saturday.

AFLW Highlights: GWS v Richmond
The Giants and Tigers clash in round six of the 2026 NAB AFLW Season

They continued to dominate through the second term with five goals in quick time to hold what looked like an insurmountable 37-point lead at the long break.
However, the Giants completely transformed after half-time, scoring 6.0 for the the third quarter, including a double from Georgia Garnett, to give themselves a glimmer of hope at the final change.

Rising Suns flex their muscles against winless Dons

ESSENDON’S search for its first win of the season continues after the Bombers fell to Gold Coast by 41 points at Windy Hill on Sunday, 7.9 (51) to 1.4 (10).
Gold Coast took control early, keeping Essendon goalless in the first half and taking a 20-point lead into the main break.

Establishing an early advantage with the breeze at their backs, the Crows were never headed and snapped a seven-game losing streak against the Lions to win 5.9 (39) to 4.6 (30).

Their third win of the season was sealed midway through the final term when exciting youngster India Rasheed nailed her left foot shot from 30m to kick the game’s only goal against the wind.
Adelaide deserved its win, dominating at clearance (35-14) and having slightly more polish than the hosts, who battled hard, but were let down by skill errors.
